newsitem.title: UK: Spend at UK tourist attractions totals 1.1 bln stg.
newsitem.headline: Spend at UK tourist attractions totals 1.1 bln stg.

text.p: Spending at UK tourist attractions rose six percent to a record 1.1 billion stg in 1995, the country's national tourist boards said in a report.
"Creative marketing, improved facilities and good weather encouraged more people to enjoy the UK's wealth of tourist attractions in 1995," said English Tourist Board chief executive Tim Bartlett.

"Prospects for 1996 look even better with the opening of world class attractions, including the Royal Armouries Museum in Leeds and Legoland, near Windsor and the National Sea Life Centre in Birmingham."

Theme park Alton Towers was the most popular pay attraction for the fourth year running, totalling 2.7 million visits. Waxwork exhibition Madame Tussauds and the Tower of London were just behind it in the pecking order. Alton Towers and Tussauds are part of the Pearson group.
Blackpool beach was the most popular free site, pulling in 7.3 million visitors.
